name: Cryo-FIB lamella milling of vitrified yeast on AutoGrids in an Aquilos DualBeam with stage and shield at -180 °C
plain_name: Carve a thin window through a frozen cell with an ion beam
description: Plunge-frozen cells on 3 mm grids clipped into Cryo-FIB AutoGrids are coated with organometallic and sputtered platinum and milled with a 30 kV ion beam (300 to 30 pA) into lamellae thinner than 200 nm, with the stage and anti-contamination shield at -180 °C under vacuum, for subsequent cryo-electron tomography.
keywords: Carve a thin window through a frozen cell with an ion beam

sources.citation: Gemin O, Gluc M, Rosa H, et al. (2024). Ribosomes hibernate on mitochondria during cellular stress. Nature Communications. doi:10.1038/s41467-024-52911-4
Zhang Y, Nandy B, Sader K, Russo CJ, Löwe J (2025). Foam film vitrification for cryo-EM. Nature Communications. doi:10.1038/s41467-025-61270-7
Thermo Scientific Aquilos 2 Cryo-FIB datasheet DS0303 (equipment reference)

requirements.rationale: Stage and anti-contaminating shield held at -180 °C (93.15 K) during milling.
Ion/electron-beam milling and SEM imaging of vitrified samples take place in vacuum.
Specimens are standard 3 mm EM grids clipped into Cryo-FIB AutoGrids.
Grids are clipped in cold nitrogen vapour before loading; nitrogen cooling of the cryo-stage.
